title: Flip Columns for the Most Equal Rows

concept.title: Rows that are equal or opposite belong together
body: A matrix of 0s and 1s is given. In one move you flip a whole **column** (every 0 becomes 1 and every 1 becomes 0 in it). You may do this for any set of columns, and then count the rows that consist of **one single value** (all 0 or all 1). What is the largest possible count?

Flipping a column changes the same position in every row. Two rows can be made constant **at the same time** exactly when they are **equal** or **opposite** (every bit differs): then the same flips fix both. So rows fall into classes of "equal or opposite" rows, and the answer is the size of the biggest class.

body.code:
key = tuple(bit ^ row[0] for bit in row)      # flip the whole row when its first bit is 1
count[key] += 1                                # equal or opposite rows get the same key

body: Normalising every row so that its first bit is 0 is the **canonical form** of the class. In C++ and Java the key can be built as a string.

statement: You are given a matrix with `n` rows and `m` columns of 0s and 1s. In one move you may flip all values of one column (0 becomes 1 and 1 becomes 0). You may flip any number of columns. After the flips, count the rows in which all values are equal (all 0 or all 1). Print the largest count you can reach.
inputFormat: The next `n` lines have `m` values (0 or 1) each.
outputFormat: Print the largest number of equal rows.

examples.note: Flip the first two columns: the rows become 1 1 0, 1 1 1 and 0 0 0: two rows are constant.

hints: A row can be made constant by flips only when the flipped columns match its pattern.
Two rows can be made constant together when they are equal or opposite.
Turn every row into a canonical form (flip it if its first bit is 1) and count the equal keys.

starter.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n, m = map(int, input().split())
g = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(n)]

# Your code here

explanation: Rows that are equal or opposite can be made constant together. Normalising each row so that its first value is 0 gives the same key to the rows of one class; the largest class is the answer.
solution.complexity: Time O(n * m) on average, space O(n * m).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n, m = map(int, input().split())
g = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(n)]

count = {}
for row in g:
    key = tuple(bit ^ row[0] for bit in row)
    count[key] = count.get(key, 0) + 1
print(max(count.values()))
